key_insight: A high-throughput DFT search identified 58 CuI-based ternary compounds as promising p-type transparent conductors, revealing that tetrahedral Cu coordination and halide chemistry can still support the chemical modulation of the valence band.
engineering_relevance: These candidates could enable better transparent electrodes for transparent electronics and tandem photovoltaics by expanding the design space beyond conventional oxide-based p-type TCMs.
method: Minima hopping method used to explore X–Cu–I ternary structures.
DFT screening applied for thermodynamic stability, optical transparency, and light hole effective mass.
Chemical modulation of the valence band (CMVB) rules were revisited using the computed dataset.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 58 candidate p-type TCMs, including 49 previously unreported materials and 20 degenerate semiconductors with intrinsic hole carriers, with Cu2FI2 highlighted as a strong example.
watch_item: The results are computationally predicted, so experimental synthesis, defect control, and stability under operating conditions still need validation.
paper_title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors
